title: Hire a Facebook Ads Expert: Where to Find One and What to Ask
summary: Where to hire a Facebook ads expert: agencies, creative studios and consultants compared, plus the account, tracking and budget checks to run before you sign.
body_markdown:
## How do you vet a Facebook ads expert?


Four checks separate real capability from a sales pitch. Ask for each one in writing before you sign.


**Partner status.** Ask whether the agency holds a Meta Business Partner badge, and what the badge covers. Meta's[Business Partners page](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing-partners) says qualifying companies receive a badge and that eligibility varies by solution type. When we checked on October 27, 2026, that page explained how companies apply but we did not find a public partner search on it, so ask the agency to name its solution type and put the claim in the contract. Our[guide to Meta Business Partner status](https://knowlify.com/articles/does-it-matter-if-meta-ads-agency-is-meta-business-partner) has the detail.


**Account ownership.** Keep the ad account, pixel and Pages in your own business portfolio, and give the agency access rather than ownership. Meta's[business-to-business guide](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management/guides/business-to-business) describes the owning business adding an agency for specific tasks, such as advertise and analyze, and notes that an agency cannot grant access to assets it holds only as an agency. When the account is yours, changing agencies means swapping access, not rebuilding campaigns.


**Tracking.** Ask who sets up the[Conversions API](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api) and who fixes events when they stop arriving. Meta describes it as a connection between your marketing data and its systems, used to optimize targeting and measure outcomes. A provider that cannot name the person who owns this setup is harder to hold to account for results.


**Concept count.** Ask how many original concepts arrive each month, not how many files. Meta's[creative diversification guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/demystifying-creative-diversification) separates diversification from iteration, and gives two ads with identical visuals but different text calls to action as an example of iteration. Twelve hook swaps on one script are closer to one concept than to twelve, so price per concept as well as per ad.


## What does it cost to hire a Facebook ads expert?


Add three lines together before you compare providers: media, the agency fee and the cost of making the ads. Meta's[minimum budgets help page](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) says Ads Manager requires a minimum budget for each campaign or ad set, that it varies by country and objective, and that it shows an alert when a budget is too low. As of October 2026, the same page says that if you set a cost per result goal, your daily budget should be at least five times that goal.


The Meta floor is small. Meta's[ad pricing page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/pricing) recommends starting with at least $5 and says the advertiser sets the daily or lifetime budget, so media is always a separate line from any fee.


Agency fees vary by model. As of October 2026, Chamber Media says to expect about $5K to $10K a month at minimum, and Top Growth Marketing's[Facebook ads agency page](https://topgrowthmarketing.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) lists fees of $2,000 to $10,000 a month in its FAQ for DTC ecommerce brands spending $5,000 to $500,000 a month on ads. Most agencies publish nothing, so ask for the fee in writing and what it includes.


A fee that is twice your media budget leaves little to test with, however good the sample ads look.


## What should you ask before you sign?


Bring these questions to the first call:


- Which solution type does the Business Partner badge cover, and does it match what I am buying?
- Which business owns the ad account, pixel and data, and what happens to access when the contract ends?
- Who sets up and fixes tracking, and who checks it each month?
- How many original concepts a month, and how many cutdowns or hook swaps are included?
- Does the price include media, the management fee, creative, revision rounds and usage rights?


If your goal is leads, ask one more question. Meta's[lead ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/lead-ads) lists lead verification such as an SMS passcode or work email, CRM connections, and an option to optimize for lead quality on instant forms. Ask whether the provider plans the form and the follow-up, or only the video.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for a steady flow of finished Facebook and Instagram video ads, with optional Meta campaign management.
- Decide which of the three costs you are buying: media, management and creative.
- Check the partner badge, the ad account owner, tracking and the monthly concept count before you sign.
- Meta enforces a small minimum budget that varies by country and objective, so the agency fee decides whether a small budget works.
- Brighter Click, Voy Media, MuteSix, Chamber Media and Hey Digital cover other needs, from campaign management to B2B SaaS.


## FAQ


### Should I hire a Facebook ads coach or an agency?


A coach teaches your team to run the account, while an agency runs the work for you. A coach fits when you have someone who will act on the advice and need a plan. An agency fits when you need ads made, tested and managed, and you do not have the people or time to do it.


### Can I hire a Facebook ads agency with only $1,000 a month in ad spend?


Meta's own floor is small, so the limit is usually the agency's. Chamber Media says it is difficult to grow on paid platforms when spending less than $5K for local brands. As of October 2026,[LYFE Marketing](https://www.lyfemarketing.com/facebook-advertising-services/) publishes image ad plans from $500 a month with a $300 setup fee, and its plan table lists $500 to $1,000 of monthly ad spend on that plan, so compare its scope with your media budget.


### Where can I hire a creative strategist for Facebook ads?


Look for an agency that names the role in its scope, or a creative-only studio that plans concepts for your buyer. Ask who chooses the angle for each test and who reads the results back into the next brief. Meta's diversification guidance recommends ads that are truly different in look, feel, storyline and message rather than minor edits of one ad, which makes a useful checklist for what a strategist should deliver.


### How do I hire a media buyer for Meta ads?


Ask for a named person, the account structure they plan to build and the reporting cadence they will use. Keep the ad account in your own business portfolio, so that changing buyers means changing access rather than rebuilding campaigns. Meta's business-to-business guide describes that arrangement.
